name: Gorillas Direct

pitch_detail.notes: Splitter cracks, corners, slab sections, and the exposed 'Monkey Traverse'

rappel_detail.notes: The one rappel of the descent, on a single rope. It is optional: below it, downclimb to the bivy sites at Stuart Pass.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed anchor on the large bench
rappel_detail.station: Descending the West Ridge’s main gully, scramble and downclimb, then break skier’s right onto a large bench; the fixed anchor is there.

rappels: One optional single-rope rappel from a fixed anchor on the bench skier’s right of the West Ridge’s main gully, then downclimb to Stuart Pass
descent_text: Follow the West Ridge to the summit, or descend via the main gully with scrambling and downclimbing, breaking right on a large bench with a single-rope rappel option, before reaching Stuart Pass bivy sites.
approach: From the Esmeralda/Lake Ingalls Trailhead at the end of FS-9737, hike the Ingalls Way Trail up switchbacks past several waterfalls. For the Cascadian Couloir and South Headwall, turn right onto the Longs Pass Trail at the junction about 1.7 miles in, climb to Longs Pass (about 6,250 ft) near mile 2.9, and descend the rocky climbers' trail on the far side to Ingalls Creek, cross on a log bridge, and follow the climbers' path up the meadow into the base of the Cascadian Couloir (South Headwall lies further up-basin via the same drainage). For West Ridge, the North Ridge routes, and the West Face Wall (Gorillas in the Mist / Gorillas Direct / King Kong), instead stay on the Ingalls Way Trail over Ingalls Pass (about 6,500 ft, roughly mile 3) and continue past Ingalls Lake toward Stuart Pass, then follow the climbers' trail onto the talus shoulder below Stuart's West Ridge and contour northwest to Goat Pass (7,600 ft) — the West Face Wall with the Gorillas routes sits in the amphitheater roughly midway between Stuart Pass and Goat Pass, while West Ridge and North Ridge climbers continue over or along Goat Pass toward their respective start points. Camping is common near Goat Pass or down at Ingalls Creek depending on the objective. The North Ridge routes can also be reached from the opposite (Mountaineer Creek) side.
overview: An eight-pitch alpine trad route on Mount Stuart's West Face Wall between Goat and Stuart Pass, following splitter cracks and exposed traverses, including the notable 'Monkey Traverse,' to a headwall finish.
beta: Eight pitches progress from the base through corners and slab sections, across the exposed horizontal 'Monkey Traverse,' and up to the headwall, on sustained crack and corner terrain.
gear: Alpine trad rack: alien/TCU to #4 cams
fa: Sol Wertkin, Jens Holsten & Mark Westman, 2011
face: West Face Wall (between Goat Pass and Stuart Pass)
